questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It being a lively city, lots of young people to hang out with and it being close by train to a lot of cool places to visit.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing experience. The city was and amazing and had so much more to offer than I first anticipated. Also the social community was great and I was able to see so much of northern italy and travel around in switzerland.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. If we had any questions we just reached out to our UNIMI coordinator and we got the help we needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got e-mails about where to pick up our student cards and how we were to get the signature for our arrival papers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The only thing being a bit confusing was picking classes at the very beginning and making sure you had a weekly schedule that did not overlap. It was one's own responsibility to figure out and maybe it would have been nice to have just a bit more guidance here. However, when you're multiple people in the same situation, you figure it out and help each other, so it was never really a problemn.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not that easy. It takes some time to figure out and you need to be careful with scammers. Also, Milan is quite expensive to live in (similar to Copenhagen) and they also charge pretty big security deposits.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend finding students who have previously studied in Milan and ask for their landlord.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was ok but again the apartments are expensive in Milan and also not that modern or in good condition (classic italian)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit hard in the beginning as you don't recieve that much guidance on this proces. Also you're able to go to different classes and "try them out" before making the official registration. However, it was different from teacher to teacher how long this process/opportunity was in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You try out classes as you wish in the beginning and then you register for the specific classes on UNIMIA (the most important website to know if studying at Statale). Some teachers also required our signature on a piece of paper during class in the beginning.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The teachers would help if we asked for it. Also our university coordinator could answer questions via e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes that I wanted except from one, as this specific course was not created this semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out different courses before making your final decision and talk to other students about how they make their schedule work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most of the courses was interessting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses is very low compared to UCPH. It was a common experience and it was not hard to get good grades in any of the courses I chose.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is different in the way that they expect more engagement from the students. Also there's a lot of oral presentations throughout the semester and activities such as mock trials, class discussions, role plays, etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Gender Justice, Cultural Diversity and Human Rights Law, International Criminal Law, Comparative Contract Law, Public and Private Partnership for Sustainable Development.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Each of the above except Cultural Diversity and Human Rights Law !! The course is not hard but the teacher was very uncomfortable throughout the entire semester,

questions.answer: Security Deposit for the apartment was way more than we expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping was less expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's plenty of opprotunities if you want to engage in the international community (fx ESN)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of different sports clubs and student activities throughout fx ESN

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any official clubs or anything through the university but we made our own student dinner club, etc., which was a nice concept throughout the semester.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Except expploring Milan I reccomend to travel around!! it's so easy and pretty cheap if you go by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat easy to get used to / adapt to the italian culture, but a bit harder to feel truly integrated in it. Italians are not very good a english, so it was really a struggle everytime you were to talk to someone or even just to order food at restaurants, going to the taylor, etc.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn italian if you can.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That everything is less structured in Italy and that time/punctuality isn't really a thing. Everyone is late for everything and you can't really say anything about it, because it's just rooted in their culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The more openness to people when fx going out. People are not as reserved as in Denmark

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The academic level is way lower than in Denmark. The teachers are quite hard to understand because of the language barrier. The city is amazing and great to be young in, especially if you enjoy going out a lot.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made and all of the cool places I got to visit.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out housing and dealing with our landlord.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
